after.asserts: 1.3 Consider any $(n,M)$ code with $M\ge2$, uniform message $J$, output states $\omega_m=\bigotimes_i\rho_{x_i(m)}$, decoding outcome $\widehat J$, and average error $e$. The Holevo measurement bound [F3] gives $I(J;\widehat J)\le\chi(\{1/M,\omega_m\})$. Applying Fano [F8] and the finite mutual-information identity [F9], with $H(J)=\ln M$, yields $(1-e)\ln M\le\chi(\{1/M,\omega_m\})+\ln2$. For $M=1$, [F2] gives $\chi(\{1,\omega_1\})=S(\omega_1)-S(\omega_1)=0$, so the inequality is $0\le\ln2$. [F1, F2, F3, F8, F9, given, algebra, cases]

Its threshold is $S(\rho_p)=h(p)$ in nats; dividing by $\ln2$ converts the logarithmic code-dimension rate to bits, hence to qubits sent per source qubit. The endpoint rates are zero, while $p=1/2$ gives $\ln2$ nats, or one qubit per source qubit. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra, cases] ∎

after.asserts: 2.1 For either input $|0\rangle$ or $|1\rangle$, the squared inner products with $|+\rangle$ and $|-\rangle$ are both $1/2$ by [F3]. Hence every joint input-output probability is $1/4$, and each marginal probability is $1/2$. The finite mutual-information sum in [F2] is therefore $\sum_{x,y}(1/4)\ln((1/4)/((1/2)(1/2)))=0$. This is strictly below $\ln2$ from step 1.1, while still satisfying the Holevo upper bound [F4]. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

after.asserts:
The cellulation has $L^2$ vertices, $2L^2$ edges, and $L^2$ faces. The
condition $L\ge3$ ensures that the four edges in each star and face are
distinct, and that every edge has two distinct endpoints and two distinct
incident faces. The vertex-edge graph joins vertices joined by an edge. The
face-adjacency graph joins faces sharing an edge; both graphs are connected.

after.asserts: 1.1 Set $d=L=3$. By [F2], the planar code has Z distance $3$ and X distance $4$, and encodes one qubit. For the toric code, [F3] gives the lower bound $3$ for every nontrivial logical Pauli, while [F5] supplies a nontrivial three-edge representative of each pure species. before.result: F^dagger F=I; P2=[[u^2,uv],[uv,v^2]], P2^2=P2, rank(P2)=1, and P1 P2 P1=phi^-2 P1.

after.calculation: With u=phi^-1 and v=phi^-1/2, F=[[u,v],[v,-u]], P1=diag(1,0), and P2=F^-1 P1 F.
after.result: F^dagger F=I; P2=[[u^2,uv],[uv,v^2]], P2^2=P2, rank(P2)=1, and P1 P2 P1=phi^-2 P1.
after.asserts: 1.2 The matrix $F$ is real symmetric and satisfies $u^2+v^2=1$; its off-diagonal entries in $F^2$ cancel because $uv-vu=0$, so $F^\dagger F=F^2=I$. Multiplication gives $P_2=F^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}F=\begin{pmatrix}u^2&uv\\uv&v^2\end{pmatrix}=ww^\mathsf T$ for $w=(u,v)^\mathsf T$. Since $w^\mathsf T w=1$, $P_2^2=w(w^\mathsf T w)w^\mathsf T=P_2$; also $\det(P_2)=u^2v^2-(uv)^2=0$ and $P_2\ne0$, so its rank is one and it is not invertible. [F1, F3, given, algebra]
